summary: Retain vertical red-green slices, independent expected values, and agreed behavioral seams; calibrate whether a test earns its cost and explain seam choices.

supporting_disposition.reason: Retain behavioral versus implementation-coupled and tautological examples; explain assertions that genuinely represent boundary contracts.
Retain external-boundary substitution and domain-shaped operations; distinguish doubles from verified production semantics.
Preserve source UI metadata and invocation policy exactly.
Retain Matt Pocock MIT attribution in every refactored package.

deltas.change: Ask whether the change has meaningful behavior and an independent oracle before adding tests.
deltas.reason: Mechanical changes can induce tautological tests.
deltas.tradeoff: Some work is verified by type/build/manual checks rather than a new test.

deltas.change: Reuse existing seam agreement and explain catches, misses, and cost for new choices.
deltas.reason: A label-only seam question transfers expert judgment to the user without help.
deltas.tradeoff: A new seam proposal includes a little more explanation.

deltas.change: Require observing the intended red failure, not just creating a test before code.
deltas.reason: An import error or already-green assertion does not establish sensitivity.
deltas.tradeoff: Each meaningful slice includes an explicit execution.

deltas.change: Preserve separate structural review while allowing necessary local cleanup under green tests.
deltas.reason: Broad redesign should not derail the loop, but an absolute ban can accumulate avoidable duplication.
deltas.tradeoff: This deliberately differs from the source's strict review-only refactoring rule.

deltas.change: Qualify blanket bans on call counts and database observations by the actual contract.
deltas.reason: A notification boundary may promise exactly one send; a persistence interface may be the real public contract.
deltas.tradeoff: Requires understanding the seam rather than matching forbidden syntax.
